claim: On a private or transit virtual interface the default is 100 routes each for IPv4 and IPv6 per BGP session from on-premises to AWS; if you advertise more route prefixes than your configured allocations, the BGP session goes idle and is reported DOWN. The quotas row also says prefix controls can raise the allocation up to 1,000 each.
question: How many routes can you advertise per BGP session on a private or transit virtual interface by default, and what happens when you advertise more?

values.spoken: one hundred each for IPv4 and IPv6

qualifiers.scope: per BGP session on a private or transit virtual interface, from on-premises to AWS
qualifiers.condition: the 1,000 each for IPv4 and IPv6 is reached only with inbound prefix controls, which are not examinable yet

evidence.quote:
| Routes per Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) session on a private virtual interface or transit virtual interface from on-premises to AWS.
If you advertise more route prefixes than your configured allocations for IPv4 and IPv6 over the BGP session, the BGP session will go into an idle state and be reported with BGP session status DOWN. | Default of 100 each for IPv4 and IPv6. Can be increased [using prefix controls](prefix-controls.md) up to 1,000 each for IPv4 and IPv6. | Contact your Solutions Architect (SA) or Technical Account Manager (TAM) for further assistance. |

note: d12-043. Examinable value is 100; prefix controls up to 1,000 (2026-08-20) are not examinable yet and have their own change fact.
